title: Edge Middleware JWT Validation Infinite Redirect Loop
businessContext: A B2B SaaS platform deployed Next.js Edge Middleware for authentication. Immediately after deployment, all enterprise users logging into `/dashboard` receive a `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` browser error.
problemStatement: The middleware intercepts all requests, checks for a session token cookie, and if invalid or expired, redirects to `/login`. However, `/login` itself was not excluded in the middleware matcher config or route check. When the user was redirected to `/login`, the middleware ran again, found no cookie, and redirected to `/login` infinitely.
constraints: Public routes (`/login`, `/signup`, `/api/auth`, `/_next`, `/favicon.ico`) must be excluded from authentication redirects.
Must properly forward cookies and path headers using `NextResponse.next()`.
Redirect URL must preserve original destination query parameter (e.g. `/login?from=/dashboard`).
candidateTasks: Identify the missing route exclusion condition causing `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`.
Configure the matcher regex to exclude `/_next/static`, `/_next/image`, `favicon.ico`, and public auth routes.
Attach `?redirectUrl=` parameter so user returns to target page after login.

testCases.name: Prevents infinite redirect loop and allows public routes
testCases.explanation: Safely protects private paths while permitting public and static routes.

alternativeApproaches: Using NextAuth.js (Auth.js) built-in authorized callback middleware.
Validating JWT signature cryptographically using jose library inside Edge runtime.
commonMistakes: Not excluding Next.js static asset chunks: Every JS and CSS chunk request gets redirected to /login, breaking styles and hydration.
Checking cookies via client-side JavaScript document.cookie instead of HTTP-only cookies in middleware.
